I have the VA as my primary medical care, my wife has TRICARE retiree, my kids are all enrolled in workplace healthcare plans. The performance record of appointment timeframes of the VA (yes, months) is far better than the three other managed healthcare plans the rest of my family is enrolled in.  Are there complaints and nuisances around certain aspects of my VA healthcare? Of course there is. Am i enrolled at one of the best places for VA healthcare that I’ve seen? Also yes (Orlando, FL). 

I’ve learned quite a bit over the years: 1) always advocate for yourself and never treat the staff in a loud or expletive manner. 2) never depart an outpatient clinic without making your next appointment at that clinic (especially your Primary care clinic). 3) do not let more than a year lapse between appointments at any specialty clinic you are referred to, you have to keep a relationship there to avoid “resetting” the cycle… failure to do so will result in waiting for another “intake” appointment at that clinic. 4) hearing aids are paid for and fully covered for those that need them, the difference between an audiologist in the community and an audiologist at the VA is that way more people (almost 100%) at the VA who have a regular relationship with the audiology department will walk out with hearing aids, this is not the case in the community, so scheduling at that clinic will back up a bit. 5) there is a small group in the administrative department called ombudsmen, if you have difficulties, contact them. It may not be the magic you are seeking, but they are the folks who can cut right to the heart of the issue and give you answers, whether you like them or not. 6) the secure messaging system can get you results, be courteous, sometimes it can assist you in having your primary care doctor fix minor things, often it can get someone to call you to set up an appointment (I rarely attempt to call them as their phone network stays busy), and it can act as a “receipt” of sorts when you send a message and they reply (I’ve watched this in action and receipts sometimes matter). 7) There are second opinions and the VA not only allows for this, it often encourages this. 8) The VA pharmacy program formulary is robust, but they do have strict rules. There are times when your doctor has to write a hand script for something non-formulary, it will cost you out of pocket to get that specific medicine, there are discount programs to bring the price of it down, this is a normal part of life when it comes to prescriptions. This is also VERY rare. 9) ALWAYS FOLLOW-UP. 10) As was the case when you were in the active military, “no one gives a s@@t about your life and career more than you do, act like it and advocate for yourself, because in most cases no one else will or can”.

Complaints: 1) I wish that the VA app would tell me what clinic I have my appointments in, it doesn’t, when I ask about it, it has something to do with privacy issues in the app? 2) I wish the clinics had the ability to email or message for appointments and issues (like appointment cancellations), because the only contact style they are allowed is by voice calling me, it’s almost always between the hours of 10am and Noon, and I’m usually in a meeting at work when the calls come. Contacting them back is usually all but impossible (see my note on that above). And given the amount of appointments I’m tied into now, these calls happen two to three times a week. 3) The VA is not used to people who work full-time in their healthcare network… availability and hours for disabled veterans who maintain employment is a concern. 

These are minor things compared to the issues the rest of my family deal with when navigating their way through their own managed healthcare plans. Overall, I feel that the VA is the best healthcare coverage out there so long as I keep my expectations managed and my patience intact, and yes, I’m friends with my ombudsman, even away from the hospital, she’s a Veteran
